record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: Let G be the minimal free resolution of a finitely generated module over a complete intersection. Can the Eisenbud operators on G be chosen so that they commute asymptotically, after ignoring a sufficiently long initial segment of the resolution?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(Q,\mathfrak{n})$ be a regular local ring (or a polynomial ring over a field) and let $f_1,\dots,f_c \in \mathfrak{n}^2$ be a regular sequence. Set $R = Q/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$, a complete intersection of codimension $c$. Let $M$ be a finitely generated $R$-module and let $G \colon \cdots \to G_{n+1} \xrightarrow{\partial} G_n \xrightarrow{\partial} \cdots \to G_0 \to M \to 0$ be its minimal free resolution over $R$. 

Choose a lifting $\widetilde{G}$ of $G$ to a sequence of free $Q$-modules with differential $\widetilde{\partial}$ satisfying $\widetilde{\partial}^{\,2} = \sum_{j=1}^{c} f_j\, t_j$, where the chain endomorphisms $t_j \colon \widetilde{G} \to \widetilde{G}$ of degree $-2$ induce, after reduction modulo $(f_1,\dots,f_c)$, the Eisenbud operators $\chi_j \colon G \to G$ of degree $-2$ on the resolution $G$. It is classical that the $\chi_j$ commute up to homotopy.

Question: Can the Eisenbud operators $\chi_1,\dots,\chi_c$ on $G$ be chosen so that they commute strictly (on the nose), i.e., $\chi_i \chi_j = \chi_j \chi_i$ for all $i,j$, after truncating $G$ by discarding a sufficiently long initial segment (i.e., for the operators restricted to $G_{\geq N}$ for some $N \gg 0$)?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of this conjecture about asymptotic strict commutativity of Eisenbud operators on minimal free resolutions over complete intersections. The classical fact that Eisenbud operators commute up to homotopy is well-documented, but whether they can be chosen to commute strictly after a sufficiently long initial truncation does not appear to be confirmed as solved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Resolutions and Cohomology over Complete Intersections
status_evidence.snippet: Eisenbud operators are chain maps defined uniquely up to homotopy, and they commute up to homotopy.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references establish commutativity of Eisenbud operators only up to homotopy, not strictly; no resolution of the asymptotic strict commutativity question is indicated.

status_evidence.title: Minimal Free Resolutions over Complete Intersections (Peeva)
status_evidence.snippet: Periodicity and structural results about minimal free resolutions over complete intersections via Eisenbud operators.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of the area discuss Eisenbud operators but do not record a proof of strict asymptotic commutativity.
